_README: OPTIONAL cold-start opinion. Never fetched at runtime - edit by hand, or generate from a leaderboard whenever you like. tier 0=avoid, 1=neutral (default), 2=good, 3=preferred. It only breaks ties between a model and ONE CATEGORY nothing is yet known about: the moment that category has even one real result, its own evidence takes over and this is ignored for it - so this can never override real results. 'tiers' is an OPTIONAL per-category override (keys: coding, reasoning, research, general, fast) for a model whose strengths differ by task; a category not listed there falls back to the flat 'tier'. Only 'tier' is required - add 'tiers' only for a model you actually have per-category opinion on. Delete this file and nothing breaks.

_EXAMPLE_a-model-strong-at-code-weak-at-.note: illustrative only - not a real model. 'coding' and 'reasoning' use their own tier; every other category (general, fast) falls back to the flat tier (2)
